title: Measured Twice
logline: In the weeks before the New Year, a tailor takes orders from a student who fears being looked down on, a mother dressing her children to impress, and a man who just wants a decent shirt.
human_question: Can you tell, from the outside, whether someone is dressing to be safe or dressing to be admired?

situation.what_happens: In the busiest weeks of a tailor's year, a run of customers order clothes for the same season and the same festival. The measuring, the chalking and the stitching are identical for each of them. What differs is what each person says, mostly unasked, about why they want it: to not be looked down on at a relative's house, to have children who are noticed, to own one shirt that is not falling apart. The tailor writes all of it down the same way and gets on with the work.
situation.who_is_involved: A tailor at the peak of a seasonal trade; the customers who pass through in a few weeks, among them a young person anxious about how they will be received, a parent dressing children for display, and someone simply replacing what has worn out; whoever helps in the shop.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the customers, how they will be seen at an occasion they cannot skip, and money spent that is not spare money. For the tailor, a year's margin compressed into a few weeks, and promises that have to be kept. For the film, the standing risk of sorting living people into good wanting and bad wanting, which is exactly what it must not do.
situation.how_it_unfolds: A tailoring season builds to a wall: orders taken freely at first, then a backlog, then the last days when something has to give. It ends with garments collected, altered, or not finished in time. Which customers choose to say anything about their reasons, and whether a reason turns out to be simpler than it first looked, is decided by them.

concept_merge.why_together: C005 contributes the line the sources themselves draw: fine clothes are listed among the everyday occasions on which greed-rooted minds arise, and then the same act is separated by aim, so that dressing to look beautiful, to attract, or to seem superior is counted one way, while dressing to cover the body and keep off cold, heat and insects is not counted as unwholesome. C004 contributes what makes it a film rather than an argument: a finished garment is a thing seen as beautiful and reached for, and the reaching is what greed is named for, not the cloth.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That the difference the sources care about is invisible from outside and audible only if a person chooses to speak it. Holding an identical act steady while the reasons vary is the only honest way to show that the act is not what is being judged, and it makes plain how little anyone watching can actually conclude about anyone else.

concept_links.why: This is the digest's own example: the same order of clothes counted as greed-rooted when it is for beauty, attraction or seeming superior, and not counted as unwholesome when it is for cover and protection [C005-M:L15] [C005-M:L17] [C005-M:L19]. The digest flags one of those rulings, that wearing good clothes to escape others' contempt is not unwholesome, as notable and needing an expert check before any film leans on it, so the film may show a customer's fear of contempt but must not state the ruling as settled.

Greed is defined as the attaching that takes things to be good, beautiful or sweet [C004-M:L13], so a finished garment belongs to the sense-sphere world the sources are counting, and the film can show the object without the object being the fault.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Two people can order the very same shirt for very different reasons, and what makes it wanting is the reason inside, not the shirt. From outside, the two are indistinguishable.
what_must_be_real: The tailor's actual orders and customers' own reasons, given freely and never in answer to a question about doctrine. No customer recruited to represent a category.
position_hint: middle: the pivot of the group, where wanting stops being told by what someone does and starts being told by why.
risks: Probing customers' motives, which is intrusive however gently it is done
Presenting poverty as virtue and comfort as vice
Sorting customers into good and bad wanting on screen
Stating the source's ruling on dressing to escape contempt as settled, when the digest flags it for expert check
drop_if: No tailor or customers will speak candidly about their own reasons
Customers' reasons can only be got by leading them

connections.note: Two garments for two occasions: one choice led by other people's wanting, one sorted by the customer's own stated reasons.
Both hold one act steady and let the aim behind it vary; one in buying, one in giving.

selection.reason: The group's clearest statement that aim, not act, is what the sources sort by; grounded in the digest's own example.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
